title: Sensor Detective
learning_outcomes: Telemetry is a reading with a unit and a time

steps.instruction: Find the temperature in the coop's sensor readings.

instruction_layers.beginner: Find the temperature in the coop's sensor readings.
instruction_layers.advanced: Telemetry arrives every 10 s on tc/ct_001/sensors as temp, humidity, ammonia and more.
instruction_layers.teacher: Ask learners to write the number down.

details: Press 'Open the coop card' below (Property Twin).
Find the Temperature row on the coop's card.
Write down the number AND the unit.
steps.watch_out: Writing the unit matters: 61 °F and 61 °C are very different.

steps.instruction: Change the simulation, then read the next value.

instruction_layers.young: Make it hot, then look again!
instruction_layers.beginner: Change the simulation, then read the next value.
instruction_layers.advanced: Run "Coop too hot" and compare the reading after the cooling routine.
instruction_layers.teacher: Ask: did it change? By how much?

details: Press 'Change the temperature (simulated)' below - or open Trigger an Event.
Wait a moment for the reading to update.
steps.watch_out: Each Trigger is a new reading; they don't add together.

steps.instruction: Use the history to see what changed.

instruction_layers.young: Was it hotter or cooler before?
instruction_layers.beginner: Use the history to see what changed.
instruction_layers.advanced: A trend needs at least two readings with times; averaging three samples removes noise.
instruction_layers.teacher: Ask learners to sketch the two points on a line.

details: Read the line: Average, Min and Max over the last 24 hours.
steps.look_for: The temperature history line with min and max.
steps.watch_out: History shows a trend - one reading alone can mislead.

steps.instruction: A number needs a unit to have meaning.

instruction_layers.beginner: A number needs a unit to have meaning.
instruction_layers.advanced: °F vs °C, % for humidity, ppm for ammonia - the unit travels with the value.
instruction_layers.teacher: Ask: what if we forgot the unit?

details: Go back to the coop's card.
Look at the unit after the number: °F (degrees Fahrenheit).
Find other units on the page: % for water, ppm for ammonia.
steps.watch_out: A number without a unit has no meaning.

steps.instruction: Describe whether the value rose, fell or stayed about the same.

instruction_layers.young: Did it go up, go down or stay the same?
instruction_layers.beginner: Describe whether the value rose, fell or stayed about the same.
instruction_layers.advanced: Report: value, unit, time and change between readings.
instruction_layers.teacher: Assessment: the learner tells the reading's story in one sentence.

details: Look at the Temperature history in Analytics.
Did it rise, fall or stay about the same?
Tell the story in one sentence, with a number and a unit.
steps.look_for: Your sentence, e.g. 'It rose from 61 °F to 92 °F, then cooled to 84 °F.'
steps.watch_out: Say what changed AND by how much.
